candidate.hyperbolic_necessity: The observed train-only directed transition graph is highly asymmetric and has many singleton/sparse pair neighborhoods; a tree-like hierarchy with branching niche continuations is a plausible geometry for allocating code capacity, whereas a constant-curvature flat space has polynomial rather than exponential volume growth. The measurements do not establish hierarchy or causality, so negative curvature is a falsifiable capacity hypothesis, not a claimed fact. Literature evidence supports adjacent hyperbolic sequential modeling and hyperbolic generative item indexing, but does not verify their complete intersection.

math_definition.assignment_and_reconstruction: Let q_i=sum_{l=1}^3 C_l,k_il and q_i^sg denote stop-gradient q_i. With item set I={1,...,N}, the single reconstruction/commitment objective is L_vq=(1/N) sum_{i in I}[||h_i-q_i^sg||_2^2 + beta||h_i^sg-q_i||_2^2], beta=0.25; reduction is a mean over items and then the 32 coordinates are summed. Empty I gives zero loss and no update. Assignments are hard argmin and treated as constants in this loss; stop-gradient prevents target-depends-on-parameters circularity. Total Stage2 objective is this loss only; there is no behavior-transition loss or Stage3/ranking loss.
math_definition.curvature_and_constants: Fix c=1.0, tau=1.0, epsilon=1e-5, and clamp delta=1e-7. For c>0 define project_c(v)=v if ||v||<(1-epsilon)/sqrt(c), else ((1-epsilon)/sqrt(c))*v/max(||v||,delta). Define d_c(x,y)=arcosh_stable(1+2c||x-y||^2/((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2)))/sqrt(c), where arcosh_stable(u)=log1p((u-1)+sqrt(max((u-1)(u+1),delta))). The argument is clamped below to 1 before applying this expression. At c->0, d_c=4||x-y||^2, exp_0 is the identity, and the radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined: omit projection entirely and apply the flat-arm code path to the same unconstrained coordinates. The implementation is one parameterized path; no map is used in assignment scoring.
math_definition.encoder_coordinates: For each item, map z_i with exp_0^c(z_i)=tanh(sqrt(c)||z_i||) z_i/(sqrt(c)||z_i||), with the zero-norm value defined by continuity as z_i; then project to obtain h_i=project_c(exp_0^c(z_i)). In the c->0 limit exp is identity and projection is omitted. These h_i are ball coordinates for c>0 and the corresponding shared flat coordinates at c=0.
math_definition.flat_arm: Set c=0 in the same implementation and retain the same encoder, codebooks, dimensions, initialization, optimizer, schedule, seeds, and training budget. exp is identity, projection is omitted because its radius is undefined, and assignment distance is 4||x-y||^2. On the c>0 path assignment is directly on bounded h/residual/code coordinates without exp/log maps. Thus the scoring path uses only the specified d_c versus 4||x-y||^2 on the shared coordinates; no map is inserted in either scoring path.
math_definition.inputs_and_shapes: For N catalog items, fixed content vectors X in R^{N x d_in}; trainable content encoder f_theta maps each row to z_i in R^{32}. Three codebooks C_l in R^{256 x 32}, l in {1,2,3}; codes are vectors in the same 32-dimensional ball coordinates. Item index i is global, not request/user/batch-specific.
math_definition.residual_order: For each item i and level l, start r_i1=h_i. At level l compute distances from the CURRENT r_il to all 256 code vectors using d_c directly on their already bounded coordinates; assign k_il=argmin_k d_c(r_il,C_lk), ties to smallest k. Then subtract in the same coordinates: r_i,l+1=r_il-C_l,k_il. Do not map, project, or normalize the residual after subtraction. For c>0, codebook vectors are constrained/projected after each optimizer update to the radius; residuals are not required to be in the ball, and the stated stable distance denominator/domain clamp is applied. At c=0 the same operations apply with 4||r-C||^2. The global SID is (k_i1,k_i2,k_i3). No earlier code conditions a later code; levels use only the current residual and their own codebook.

candidate.next_item_hypothesis: Demonstrated failure: a single flat Euclidean quantization scale may allocate codes poorly for sparse, directed next-item structure, merging niche successor regions with frequent transitions. The train-only transition evidence has 339519 transitions over 323633 directed pairs and 24556 distinct items; 314605 pairs have no observed reverse (fraction 0.9266197178950221). This is evidence of asymmetry/sparsity, not proof of a causal recommender failure. Hypothesis: negatively curved residual code geometry can allocate resolution to hierarchical, branching item neighborhoods while preserving a single item-global SID. Stage3 remains the sole next-item ranker.
candidate.real_trigger_measurement: The evidence-trigger is the measured train-only transition asymmetry: no_observed_reverse_events=314605 of 339519 transitions, fraction 0.9266197178950221, alongside 323633 directed pairs and mean next-item entropy 4.844072338042215 bits. This motivates testing, but cannot establish geometry necessity or improvement.
candidate.training_only_inputs: Content embeddings and item identities for Stage2 reconstruction, plus only transitions legally visible in the train split as allowed by CLAUDE.md rule 16; this frozen mechanism does not consume transition labels. Validation is used only for registered Stage2 diagnostics, and test only for the one registered Stage3 behavioral test. No validation/test/future event, prediction-time user context, or batch composition enters fitting, code assignment targets, or loss.
